the_client_leg_check_that_would_fail_a_c:
THE SHARPEST THING THIS SLICE MEASURED, AND IT IS A FINDING ABOUT THE SUITE RATHER THAN ABOUT US. `sep-2243-client-includes-standard-headers` / `ClientMcpNameHeader_tools_call` requires a tools/call POST to carry an `Mcp-Name` header whose value is the body's `params.name`. There is no decoding anywhere in the 1793 bytes that hold both routing-header predicates end to end: the measurement is ND07, pattern `(?i)base64|Buffer\.from|decodeValue|=\?|\bdecode` over [699044, 700837], zero hits, with `mcp-name`, `params.` and `headers[` returning hits that show the sweep read the right bytes.

SO THE TWO OBLIGATIONS COLLIDE. `streamable-http.mdx:508-510` requires a client to Base64-sentinel-encode a header value that is not header-safe — a non-ASCII tool name, for instance — and :501-504 requires the server to DECODE before comparing. A client that does the first would send `Mcp-Name: =?base64?...?=` against a `params.name` that is the raw name, and `a!==i` would be true, and this check would score FAILURE on a conforming client. It scores SUCCESS at the accepted run for one reason and it is the fixture's: every tool name in the suite is header-safe, so `HeaderMirror.encode_value/1` is the identity on all of them and the encoded and raw forms coincide.

WHY IT IS RECORDED HERE AND WHAT IT IS NOT. It is why `MCP.Transport.SelfCompatibilityTest`'s REACHABILITY CONTROL member is bucket 1 under ND07 rather than carrying an edge: the check is in the right place and cannot score the behaviour, which is a fixture-and-predicate gap and not a counterpart. It is NOT a `contradicts` verdict, and the reason is C1c-iv-a's own lesson restated — a shared error code or a shared header name is not subject identity. On the inputs the check actually sees, our client and the check agree; they would disagree on an input the check never gets. A contradiction is a claim that the check's requirement is wrong, and ours is not that. It is also NOT a defect we can fix: the remedy is upstream, either decoding in the predicate or a non-header-safe name in the fixture. Recorded as a coverage finding about the suite, with the bytes, so a reader does not have to take it on trust.
